label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the review, in your voice and close to your word target. I've left two placeholders for you to fill in.

---

**One star for now: the software works, the support doesn't**

We went live on Stackhouse Cloud on October 19, 2026, on a three-year contract signed in June at $14,200 a year. For scale: Bridger Bend Community Library is one branch, two full-time staff plus volunteers, about 2,300 active cardholders.

Since October 28, our circulation system has only functioned offline on a single laptop, and our holds queue was wiped during the move. Roughly 640 holds are gone, including large-print titles our regulars request by name. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home empty-handed. Our volunteers have been recording checkouts on index cards.

Our support ticket has been open 12 days. We have received three replies, each stating the matter had been "escalated to engineering." During the sales process, our representative promised a dedicated migration specialist. What we received was a shared inbox.

Here is what I am and am not saying. The staff interface is better than what we had, and the product concept is sound. I am not reviewing the software badly. The failure is in support, and on that measure it is complete, not partial. Twelve days of silence with no working contact is not a partial failure in a library our size.

One star for now. I would revise this upward if the problem is actually fixed.

To Stackhouse leadership: I am asking for a call this week from a named person with the authority to act on it, not a ticket number and not a shared inbox. Specifically, I want to know when the holds queue is restored and what happens to the 640 cardholders whose holds disappeared. I am reachable at [email] and [phone], and I am glad to speak with your engineers directly.

To any small library weighing a Stackhouse contract: before you sign, get support response times and escalation contacts in writing. Ask what happens to patrons' hold records if a migration drops them, and what "dedicated specialist" means in the contract rather than in a sales conversation. Ask for references from libraries your size.

Our county commissioners will read this, since our line item is on the November 18 hearing agenda. I would rather describe this accurately than describe it generously and be wrong.

---

Three small things before you post:

1. Fill in the contact line. A public review asking for a callback with no way to reach you wastes the ask. Consider a Google Voice number if you don't want your personal line ringing.
2. If you have the ticket number, add it. It makes the 12-day claim checkable rather than just asserted, which matters if a commissioner's staff pulls the record.
3. Send the same text, or a condensed version, to Stackhouse leadership by email the day you post. If leadership hears it only from a public site, they can reasonably read it as an ambush. If they hear it from you first, the call request is much harder to ignore. It's also good documentation for the hearing.

One note on the hold count: you said "around 640." I wrote "roughly 640" for the same reason, because someone can check that number against your records and you want it to hold. If it's actually approximate to a wider band, soften to "several hundred."
